'''Charles Samuel Peskin''' (born April 15, 1946) is an American [[mathematician]] known for his work in the mathematical modeling of blood flow in the heart.  Such calculations are useful in the design of [[artificial heart valves]].  From this work has emerged an original computational method for [[fluid-structure interaction]] that is now called the “[[immersed boundary method]]", which allows the coupling between deformable immersed structures and fluid flows to be handled in a computationally tractable way. With his students and colleagues, Peskin also has worked on mathematical models of such systems as the [[inner ear]], arterial pulse, [[blood clotting]], [[congenital heart disease]], light adaptation in the [[retina]], control of [[ovulation]] number, control of [[plasmid]] replication, [[molecular dynamics]], and [[molecular motors]].<ref name="macarthur">{{cite web|url=http://www.macfound.org/fellows/145/|title=C.S. Peskin - MacArthur Foundation|publisher=The John D. and Catherine T. MacArthur Foundation}}</ref><ref name="birkhoff">{{cite journal |title=2003 Birkhoff Prize |journal=Notices of the AMS |volume=50 |number=4 |year=2003 |pages=471-473 |url=https://www.ams.org/notices/200304/comm-birkhoff.pdf}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |journal=MetroMath |title=Annual Meeting |year=2008 |url=http://sections.maa.org/metrony/newsletters/news2008.pdf}}</ref>

Peskin received an A.B. (1968) from [[Harvard University]] and a Ph.D. (1972) from the [[Albert Einstein College of Medicine]], [[Yeshiva University]] and shortly thereafter joined the faculty of the [[Courant Institute of Mathematical Sciences]], [[New York University]].  He has been a productive educator of applied mathematicians, and has advised more than fifty graduate students as of 2014.  Peskin is a [[MacArthur Fellow]] and a member of the [[National Academy of Sciences]], the [[Institute of Medicine]] and the [[American Academy of Arts and Sciences]].

In 1969 he married Lucille G. Bisesi. Their son Eric is the manager of High Performance Computing at New York University.<ref>[https://pdfs.semanticscholar.org/68a1/b8443899e4ba4e5e385eded9cf9a57069611.pdf Peskin, Eric R. "High-Performance Computing (HPC) at NYU."]</ref>

==Awards and honors==
*[[George David Birkhoff Prize in Applied Mathematics]] from AMS–SIAM, 2003<ref name="birkhoff"/>
*Invited speaker of the [[International Congress of Mathematicians]], 1998<ref>{{cite book|author=Peskin, Charles S.|chapter=Optimal dynamic instability of microtubules|title=Doc. Math. (Bielefeld) Extra Vol. ICM Berlin, 1998, vol. III|year=1998|pages=633–642|chapter-url=https://www.elibm.org/ft/10011618000}}</ref>
*Mayor's Award for Excellence in Science and Technology, 1994
*[[Sidney Fernbach Award]], [[Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers]] Computer Society, 1994
*Cray Research Information Technology Leadership Award for Breakthrough Computational Science, 1994
*[[Josiah Willard Gibbs Lecturer]], [[American Mathematical Society]], 1993
*New York University Margaret and Herman Sokol Faculty Award in the Sciences, 1992
*[[James H. Wilkinson Prize in Numerical Analysis and Scientific Computing]], [[Society for Industrial and Applied Mathematics|SIAM]], 1985<ref>[https://www.siam.org/prizes-recognition/major-prizes-lectures/detail/james-h-wilkinson-prize-in-numerical-analysis-and-scientific-computing James H. Wilkinson Prize in Numerical Analysis and Scientific Computing]</ref>
*MacArthur Fellowship, 1983–1988<ref name="macarthur"/>

He has also been a fellow of the [[American Academy of Arts and Sciences]] since 1994,<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.amacad.org/multimedia/pdfs/classlist.pdf|title=List of active members by class|publisher=The American Academy of Arts & Sciences}}</ref> a member of the [[United States National Academy of Sciences|National Academy of Sciences]] since 1995,<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nasonline.org/directory-entry/charles-s-peskin-zr6r9q/|title=Charles Peskin|publisher=The National Academy of Sciences}}</ref> and a member of the [[Institute of Medicine]] (now the National Academy of Medicine) since 2000.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://nam.edu/wp-content/uploads/2023/05/NAM-Member-ListingForWeb2023.pdf|title=Member listing|publisher=National Academy of Medicine|year=2023|access-date=2024-04-19 }}</ref> He is also an inaugural fellow of the [[American Mathematical Society]]<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.ams.org/notices/201305/rnoti-p631.pdf|title=Fellows of the AMS: inaugural class|publisher=The American Mathematical Society}}</ref> and the [[Society for Industrial and Applied Mathematics]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.maa.org/news/math-news/siam-names-its-inaugural-fellows-class|title=SIAM names its inaugural fellows class|publisher=The Mathematical Association of America}}</ref>
